title: Multi-Wavelength Study of a Proto-BCG at z = 1.7
question: Characterize the stellar mass, SFR, AGN bolometric luminosity, and 3.3 mm continuum origin of a z = 1.7 proto-BCG (FRII host galaxy), and search for radio galaxy-ICM interaction signatures via 1.4 GHz polarized emission.

data.sensitivity: ~9 uJy rms within primary beam half maximum

what.value: Broadband optical/IR/mm photometry of the FRII host galaxy from HST/ACS, CFHT/WIRCam, CTIO/ISPI, Spitzer/IRAC, Spitzer/MIPS, Herschel/PACS, Herschel/SPIRE, and AzTEC

evidence.loc: Broadband Optical/IR Photometry
evidence.quote: Thus, in previous works we re-analyzed the data for HST and MUSYC. As for the WIRCam and IRAC channels, we followed the same photometry measurements as described in (cite: balmaverde_2017).

evidence.quote: This value is well below than that measured on the JVLA map ($S_{1.4~\mathrm{GHz}}=315 \pm 25$ $\upmu$Jy, ref. (cite: damato_subm)), confirming that the flux density at 1.4 GHz is dominated by the AGN.

recipe.goal: Image ALMA 3.3 mm continuum and measure FRII core flux density
recipe.method: Multi-frequency synthesis continuum imaging of the three-pointing Band 3 mosaic excluding line-contaminated channels, followed by flux density measurement of the FRII core
key_parameters: Excluded velocity range: +/- 1500 km/s around z = 1.694
Briggs weighting with robust = 0.5, mfs mode at 92.04 GHz

recipe.goal: Fit the broadband optical-to-mm SED of the FRII host galaxy and derive physical parameters
recipe.method: Simultaneous three-component SED fitting (SSPs for stellar emission, dusty AGN torus, and cold dust heated by starburst) using two cold dust models (cold dust template vs. gray-body), excluding the ALMA 3.3 mm point; derive SFR, sSFR, intrinsic X-ray luminosity, gas depletion time, and SMBH accretion rate
software: SED fitting code of Fritz et al. (2006) / Feltre et al. (2012)
assumptions: Fiducial uncertainties of 20% on L_bol and L_FIR, and 30% on stellar mass following Circosta et al. (2019)
Linear L_FIR - SFR calibration of Kennicutt (1998) after subtracting AGN fraction
AGN bolometric corrections from Duras et al. (2020) and BH accretion efficiency eta = 0.3

recipe.goal: Determine the physical origin (thermal dust vs. non-thermal synchrotron) of the 3.3 mm ALMA core emission
recipe.method: Compare measured ALMA 3.3 mm flux density against gray-body and template SED predictions, and estimate non-thermal synchrotron contribution at 3 mm by subtracting SFR-driven 1.4 GHz flux from measured JVLA 1.4 GHz core flux and extrapolating to 3 mm
key_parameters: Synchrotron spectral index alpha = 0.5 - 1.0 (S_nu proportional to nu^-alpha)
assumptions: Stellar mass- and redshift-dependent L_8-1000um - L_1.4GHz relation from Delvecchio et al. (2021)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image JVLA 1.4 GHz linear polarization, fractional polarization, and magnetic field orientation
recipe.method: Calibrate instrumental cross-hand delays and leakage using unpolarized calibrator 3C147; calibrate polarization angle and fraction using in-field NVSS source J102921+051938 in two 42 MHz IFs; image Stokes I, Q, U; compute debiased linear polarization, fractional polarization, and magnetic field orientation
key_parameters: IF1 centered at 1365 MHz (42 MHz bandwidth) with tau_1 = 8.4 deg; IF2 centered at 1435 MHz (42 MHz bandwidth) with tau_2 = 5.2 deg; mean polarized fraction F = 4.73 +/- 0.3%
Briggs robust = 0.5, uv-taper < 50 klambda (~2.5 arcsec beam), blanked at 3 sigma, B-field orientation = 0.5 arctan(U/Q) + pi/2 in steps of 3 pixels
assumptions: No magnetic field wrapping between IF1 and IF2 (valid for RM < 400 deg/m^2)
